claim_reference: Adv. Funct. Mater. 2026, 36:e75639, Section 2.2, SI Section 1, Table S3 (Two-Mode Maxwell Viscoelasticity & Half-Times)

preregistration.hypothesis: Viscoelastic relaxation half-times t_1/2 up to 3,267 s can be reliably identified from a 100 s stress relaxation hold, and sigma_100 serves as a sufficient scalar proxy for relaxation kinetics.
preregistration.primary_metric: Maximum extrapolation ratio (t_half / t_obs_max), 90% confidence interval width on t_1/2 under 2% instrument noise, and kinetic divergence between identical-sigma_100 profiles.
preregistration.decision_rule: SUPPORTED if max extrapolation ratio <= 3.0 and t_1/2 90% CI width <= 20% of nominal value; WEAKENED if extrapolation ratio > 5.0 or t_1/2 90% CI width > 50%; CONTRADICTED if model is mathematically collinear / unidentifiable.

summary: Viscoelastic rheology audit severely weakens the claimed relaxation half-times. For Stiff Tumor (I1-4), the paper claims t_1/2 = 3,267 s extrapolated from an experimental hold of only 100 s -- a 32.7-fold unmeasured time extrapolation. Numerical sensitivity analysis shows that under realistic 2% rheometer noise, the 90% confidence interval for t_1/2 spans [384 s, 10000 s] (IQR = 9576 s), demonstrating complete parameter unidentifiability. Furthermore, the single-number sigma_100 proxy conceals dramatic kinetic variations: formulations with identical sigma_100 can exhibit early vs delayed relaxation pathways.
